malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Spyware module that scans the filesystem for sensitive documents and exfiltrates them to a remote server.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At installation-time, the code searches the infected machine for sensitive documents, collects them, and sends them to a remote command-and-control server, enabling data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is embedded in a trojanized installer and performs unauthorized scanning and exfiltration of user documents.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers should not search for or transmit user documents to external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise backup or document management tools may scan and upload files, but only with user consent and clear notification.
key_indicators: Document search and exfiltration in installer context
Network communication to unknown remote server

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malware module capable of taking screenshots, stealing files, capturing audio recordings, and downloading/executing further modules.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code takes periodic screenshots, records audio from the microphone, steals files from the filesystem, and communicates with a remote server to download and execute additional malicious modules.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs multiple forms of surveillance and data theft without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Linux applications do not take screenshots, record audio, or exfiltrate files without explicit user action.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote administration tools may have similar capabilities, but only with user knowledge and consent.
key_indicators: Screenshots and audio capture in background

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on Android device, when media file is received)
execution_context.file_location: malicious code within WhatsApp/Telegram media file handler

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Code that intercepts and manipulates media files received via WhatsApp/Telegram before the user views them.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a media file is received, the code intercepts the file, modifies its contents (e.g., payment details), and saves the manipulated file for the user to view, enabling fraud or misinformation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and modifying received media files in real-time is not expected behavior for messaging apps.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Messaging apps should not alter received files without user action.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Image optimization or compression may alter files, but not in a way that changes their meaning or content.
key_indicators: Real-time interception and modification of media files
Manipulation of payment or sensitive information
No user notification of file alteration

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on iOS, during app login process)
execution_context.file_location: malicious app abusing iOS URL Scheme

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious app registers for URL schemes used by other apps to intercept sensitive data during login.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malicious app hijacks URL scheme callbacks intended for legitimate apps, capturing sensitive authentication data and sending it to an attacker-controlled server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Hijacking URL schemes to intercept authentication data is a known attack vector and not legitimate app behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Apps should not register for or intercept URL schemes used by other apps for sensitive data exchange.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some apps use URL schemes for deep linking, but not for intercepting credentials.
key_indicators: Registration for third-party app URL schemes

attack_chain.action: User downloads and runs a trojanized installer for legitimate software (e.g., WinBox).
attack_chain.leads_to: Spyware is installed on the system.

attack_chain.action: Spyware searches for sensitive documents and exfiltrates them to a remote server.
On Linux, EvilGnome spyware runs in the background, taking screenshots, recording audio, and stealing files.
On Android, malicious code manipulates media files received via WhatsApp/Telegram in real-time.
On iOS, malicious app hijacks URL scheme to steal authentication data during app login.

behavioral_signatures: Installer or application scanning for and exfiltrating user documents
Background processes taking screenshots or recording audio without user interaction
Real-time modification of media files received by messaging apps
Apps registering for and intercepting third-party URL schemes
file_indicators: Unexpected binaries or modules in installer packages
Unknown background processes with access to microphone or screenshot APIs
Modified media files in WhatsApp/Telegram directories
iOS apps with overlapping URL scheme registrations
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known C2 infrastructure
Unusual data uploads following installation of new software
Connections from messaging apps to unrecognized domains
iOS apps sending authentication data to external servers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for installer or application behavior that scans and exfiltrates user files, background processes accessing audio or screenshot APIs, real-time file modifications in messaging app directories, and apps registering for or intercepting URL schemes used by other apps. Correlate with outbound network traffic to detect exfiltration or C2 communication.
